# Shippabel

> Shippabel checks apps built with AI tools, fixes what Google Play would reject, writes the store page, frames the screenshots, builds the app in the cloud and publishes it to Google Play. It is made for people who are not developers. The check is free; publishing one app costs $99, paid once.

Last updated: 2026-11-02

## What Shippabel is

Shippabel (https://shippabel.com) is a web service for people who built an app with an AI tool such as ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, Lovable, Bolt, Base44, v0 or Replit and now want it on Google Play. They do not need to know what a repository, a keystore or Android Studio is, and they do not need a Mac or any developer tools on their computer.

## What it does, in order

1. **Check (free, about 30 seconds, no account).** The person pastes a GitHub link, or uploads a zip file. Shippabel reads the code and returns a report with a readiness score from 0 to 100, the problems Google Play would reject, and the fixes.
2. **Fix.** Many problems can be fixed with one click. Changes are ordinary commits in the person's GitHub repository, so they can be reviewed and undone.
3. **Store page.** AI writes the app name, short and full description and keywords in three styles, and generates a privacy policy that Shippabel hosts. Screenshots are framed in device mockups.
4. **Build and upload.** Shippabel builds a signed Android App Bundle (AAB) in the cloud, usually in 10 to 20 minutes, and uploads it to the app's internal testing track in the person's own Google Play Console.
5. **Review status.** Shippabel tracks the review status and explains rejections in plain language.

## What Shippabel does not do

- It publishes to **Google Play only** today. Apple App Store (iOS) publishing is planned and is **not available yet**.
- Automatic conversion of a web app to an Android app works for **Vite** web apps (a common output of AI tools such as Lovable and Bolt). **Expo** apps are built as they are. **Next.js and Nuxt** apps (for example from v0) need a static export and a Capacitor setup first. Flutter and native Swift or Kotlin apps are not supported. The free check says which kind an app is.
- It does not host an app's backend or database. An Android app cannot contain a server, so a backend must run online on its own.
- It does not run Google's closed test for the person. Google requires personal developer accounts created after November 2023 to run a closed test with at least 12 testers for 14 days before an app can be released publicly. The person runs that test in their own Play Console. See https://shippabel.com/blog/google-play-12-testers-rule
- Google decides when an app goes public. Review usually takes a few days.

## Pricing

- **Free:** unlimited checks, readiness reports, an AI store page preview.
- **Ship, $99 once, per app:** one-click fixes, the full AI store page, screenshot frames, a hosted privacy policy, a cloud build and upload to Google Play, review status tracking.
- **Unlimited, $179 once:** everything in Ship for any number of apps, with priority support.
- No subscription. Google charges its own one-time $25 fee for a developer account, paid to Google.
- Refund promise: if Shippabel cannot get the app onto Google Play, the full amount is refunded.
